title: pm-dispatch skill: route cards to a thread by size and shape only; p1 sets order, not mode
body:
repo:objectstack#1 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgUkbQqRUUFSiu2HGob

## Problem

The skill sends every p1 card and every `security` card to its own card thread when the seat is a project thread, whatever the card's size:

- `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/dispatch-runbook.md:120` — `M 及以上、p1、\`security\` 卡一卡一线程`
- `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md:69` (the `mode:` row) — `席位是项目线程时 M 及以上、p1、\`security\` 一律 \`thread\``

A thread costs a fresh clone and a full re-read of `os-dev.md` before any work starts. Under the current p1-only lane order every card is p1, so even an S card pays that start-up cost. Priority says when a card runs, not how hard it is.

## Ruling

The maintainer chose "only size decides; p1 only sets order" on a decision card on 2026-11-20 (about 07:44Z), after asking 「p1，安全卡只是优先级，不代表复杂度，为什么一定要不进区？」 (07:42:03Z). The ruling record is posted as the first comment on this card; the PR's `Ruling-ref:` cites it.

## What changes

The two lines above say instead:

- S cards run as `mode:subagent`, in the seat or inside an area.
- M cards go into an area when one fits; with no fitting area, a card thread.
- One thread per card stays for big cards as `dispatch-runbook.md` already defines them (L/XL, owing full verification, or contract-changing) and for repair rounds that follow them.
- A security card under disclosure discipline still stays in the seat session (line 123 already says this; keep it).
- p1 sets order only. It never selects `mode:thread` by itself.

Check the rest of `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/**` for any other line that ties p1 or `security` to `mode:thread`, and change it the same way.

## Constraints

- `.claude/**` is governed. The PR body carries `Rule-change: ruled` and a `Ruling-ref:` line to the ruling record; the L2 record must read `Rule-change-verified: ruled`.
- Both files are at byte headroom 0 under `check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs`. Fit the new text by compressing the same file. The ruling record covers these lines only; it does not by itself raise a ceiling.

## Done when

- Neither file routes a card to `mode:thread` because of p1 or `security` alone.
- The big-card and disclosure-discipline exceptions still read as they do now.
- `check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs` passes with no ceiling raised.
